newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moody's may downgrade long-term SNCF ratings.
newsitem.headline: Moody's may downgrade long-term SNCF ratings.

text.p: Moody's said on Thursday it had placed the long-term debt ratings of French state railway SNCF (Societe Nationale des Chemins de Fer Francais) under review for possible downgrade.
SNCF's Prime-1 rating for commercial paper and the Aaa rating assigned to the debt guaranteed by the government are not under review and are confirmed, Moody's said in a statement.

"This rating action is prompted by the French government's decision to approve a draft bill that incorporates changes in the organisation of the French railways and redefines the role of the SNCF," Moody's said.
Under the terms of the bill, a new public entity would own and finance the infrastructure of the network while SNCF would operate the railway system and manage the infrastructure.
"The draft bill does not introduce a change in the legal status of the SNCF, an important factor in the present rating," the ratings agency said.
"The review will focus on the long-term implications of this reform for SNCF within the context of initiatives of the European Union to introduce market forces in rail transport," it said.
Moody's said it will also study the implications of the restructuring and the state's objectives regarding the financial position and operating performance of the SNCF.
Ratings under review are SNCF's Aaa rating for long-term senior debt and Aaa counterparty rating.
